comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C11-C14 regarding abnormal NPC proliferation in WS organoids. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with no methodological concerns raised.
Perfect agreement on claims C15-C19 regarding impaired neuronal differentiation. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED and treat them as core findings without critique.
Perfect agreement on claims C20-C24 regarding transcriptomic findings from bulk RNA-seq. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED and highlight NGS techniques as a strength.
Perfect agreement on claims C25-C29 regarding scRNA-seq findings and aberrant excitatory neurogenesis. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED and recognize them as major contributions.
Perfect agreement on claims C30-C33 regarding pseudotime analysis and developmental trajectory. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED without questioning the analysis.

Agreement on claims C34, C36-C37 regarding TTR identification and validation. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED and recognize TTR as a key discovery, though peer review also includes C60 (summary claim).

Disagreement on claims C38-C40 regarding GTF2IRD1 regulation of TTR via MAPK/ERK pathway. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, citing incomplete evidence and lack of mechanistic depth.

Disagreement on claims C41-C44 regarding TTR rescue experiments. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with strong evidence, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, stating the rescue data alone are insufficient for the proposed mechanism.
Agreement on claims C45-C50 regarding mouse model validation. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED and view the cross-species validation as a strength of the study.
Agreement on claims C51-C53 regarding mouse eNPC experiments. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED as part of the multi-model validation approach. Peer R10 also covers C54-C56.

Agreement on claims C54-C56 regarding ChIP-qPCR evidence of Gtf2ird1 transcriptional regulation of Ttr. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED without questioning the direct mechanistic evidence.

Disagreement on summary claims C57-C59, C64. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED (noting C57's synapse claim lacks direct support), while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN due to incomplete mechanistic understanding and lack of depth in the MAPK pathway evidence.
OpenEval evaluated background claims C1-C10 about WS as SUPPORTED by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C65, C66, C69-C71 (background and context claims) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature-based claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C67-C68 regarding TTR's role in neurogenesis and WS pathology as SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluated claim C72 regarding TTR as potential therapeutic target as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative and requires extensive validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.
